title: Tenanted hysteresis and bounded fallback plan for dependency trips
creator: Sofia Malik
description:
Background: We need a robust, per-tenant and per-dependency circuit-breaker system that trips predictably under load while minimizing user-visible errors. Existing global breakers are too coarse: a noisy tenant or third-party backend can cascade failures across unrelated customers. This ticket defines a design and rollout plan for: 1) tenant-scoped breakers with hysteresis and grace windows, 2) bounded fallback behaviors (model substitution, degraded features, queueing), 3) trip threshold tuning driven by SLOs (p50/p95 latency and error-rate budgets), and 4) safe multi-region failover integration.

Goals: - Implement hysteresis windows so breakers don't oscillate (trip cooldown + gradual recovery). - Allow per-tenant grace-periods and exception budgets for bursty customers. - Define fallback hierarchy (local cheap-model -> cached response -> remote routed model -> synthetic degrade) and ensure fallbacks are rate-limited and instrumented. - Surface per-tenant health and simulated "what-if" tripping in Console for SRE/SEs to validate thresholds. - Ensure rollouts can be gated via feature flags and automatic rollback on regressions.

Design notes: - Thresholds are defined as composite SLOs: rolling 5m p95 latency > X ms OR error-rate > Y% OR queue-depth > Z triggers a soft trip. - Soft trip behavior: divert a percentage of requests (configurable) to a fallback cohort instead of a hard stop; percentage increases according to sustained violation and tenant severity. - Hard trip: when soft-trip continues for N consecutive evaluation periods (default 4), route all non-critical traffic to fallbacks and reject heavy requests with structured 429/503 that include retry-after and diagnostic id. - Hysteresis: recovery requires two successive evaluation periods of metric health below the recovery threshold to avoid flip-flop. - Grace budgets: each tenant has a daily "burst allowance" that permits transient threshold breaches before soft-trip. This is stored in the Redis metastore with leaky-bucket decay. - Predictive smoothing: use exponential smoothing on error-rate and latency to avoid reacting to single large outliers. - Fallbacks prioritized: 1) cached prefix + KV response, 2) smaller quantized model hosted in-region, 3) cross-region model routing, 4) degraded structured output (reduce context or respond with summary), 5) synthetic apology with safe partial result.

Operational controls: - Feature flag per tenant and global kill-switch. - Configurable trip windows (evaluation window length, consecutive window count, backoff factor). - Canary rollout plan with traffic shaping by tenant cohorts. - Console: per-tenant breaker state, trip history, current fallback cohort percentage, and simulated trigger tool that replays recent traffic against candidate thresholds.

Telemetry & Alerts: - Emit metrics: breaker_state{tenant,dep}, fallback_ratio, soft_trip_count, hard_trip_count, simulated_triggered, trip_reason tags. - Alert when >3 tenants in a region enter hard trip within 5m. - Continuous export to incident dashboard; retention for 90 days for postmortems.

Testing & Simulation: - Create a synthetic traffic generator to exercise tenant bursts and dependency failures. - Run chaos experiments: inject high p95 latency into model-hosting pool and validate soft->hard transition and safe fallback chain. - Add unit tests for hysteresis logic and integration tests for fallback ordering.

Rollout Plan: 1) Merge backend logic behind feature flag (ENG branch), unit tests green. 2) Small canary: enable for 10 internal tenants + synthetic traffic for 48h. 3) Tune thresholds and hysteresis based on observed false positives. 4) Expand to 100 tenants in a region with monitoring. 5) Global rollout with per-region defaults and option for tenant-level overrides.

Open questions / tradeoffs: - Where to store tenant burst budgets: Redis vs. durable database? Chosen Redis for low-latency but need failover plan. - Soft-trip default percentage and growth curve: linear vs. exponential backoff. We will start with linear increments (10% every evaluation period) to limit abrupt user impact. - Should retries be attempted to a different region automatically? We'll allow cross-region routing for fallbacks but only when data residency policy permits. - How to surface helpful diagnostics in 429/503 responses without leaking sensitive info? Include a short diagnostic id and link to Console where RBAC will apply.

Acceptance criteria: - Feature flagged breaker logic merged and passes unit/integration tests. - Console shows per-tenant breaker state and simulation tool. - Canary run demonstrates <1% extra customer errors and measurable reduction in downstream cascading failures. - Playbook for SREs updated with runbooks and rollback steps.

comments: 2026-02-21 - Ethan Zhao: Initial implementation prototype for hysteresis state machine pushed to feature/tenant-breaker. Basic unit tests added. Need review for expiration semantics of burst budgets.

2026-02-25 - Priya Nair (PM): Adjusted goals to require a Canary window of at least 48 hours and explicit SLO verification before broader rollout. Also requested that Console simulator show percentile breakdowns.

2026-03-01 - Lucas Rivera (SRE): Ran chaos injection in staging; observed soft-trip behaved as expected but recovery was too slow due to conservative hysteresis settings. Suggested reducing consecutive-window requirement from 4 to 2 for staging canary and keep 4 for prod.

2026-03-05 - Security review (Anika Shah): Raised note about diagnostic ids potentially exposing tenant linkage; recommend tokenized correlation ids and RBAC gating on Console links. Marked security_review_required = true.

2026-03-09 - Ethan Zhao: Updated implementation to use tokenized diagnostic ids and moved burst budgeting into Redis with fallback to DB on cache miss. Added integration test for Redis failover behavior. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/7812

2026-03-12 - Sofia Malik: QA smoke passed in canary (10 internal tenants). Observed fallback ordering correctly prefers in-region quantized model. Next: expand to 100 tenants next week and monitor trip_reason distributions.
